name: General requirements
note: Sets the architecture rather than asking for disclosures — double materiality, reporting boundary, value chain, time horizons, and how to apply the topical standards. Nothing is filed against it directly, which is why its disclosure count is zero, but every judgement in this tool is made under it.

name: General disclosures
note: Applies in full regardless of the materiality assessment — the one standard a preparer cannot screen out. The twelve named disclosure requirements are listed. ESRS 2 also carries the minimum disclosure requirements for policies, actions, targets and metrics (MDR-P/A/T/M), which are not separate DRs but are applied through each topical standard, so they are not counted here.
dr_source: The twelve named disclosure requirements of ESRS Set 1 — BP-1 and BP-2, GOV-1 to GOV-5, SBM-1 to SBM-3, IRO-1 and IRO-2 — taken from published summaries of the standard. The minimum disclosure requirements (MDR-P/A/T/M) are applied through each topical standard rather than filed against ESRS 2 directly, so they are not counted as separate requirements here.

Strategy, business model and value chain

Process to identify and assess material impacts, risks and opportunities
Disclosure requirements covered by the sustainability statement

name: Climate change
note: Assessed as material by almost every preparer, and the only topical standard where omission attracts an explicit explanation requirement. E1-6 is cross-linked to the GHG inventory in the evidence ledger — if an inventory exists, that DR already has evidence and its data quality score travels with it.
dr_source: The nine disclosure requirements of ESRS Set 1, taken from published summaries. E1-6 remains the gross Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions requirement under the revised 2026 standard, which is why the cross-link to the GHG inventory still holds.

Targets related to climate change mitigation and adaptation
Energy consumption and mix
Gross Scopes 1, 2, 3 and total GHG emissions
GHG removals and mitigation projects financed through carbon credits
Internal carbon pricing
Anticipated financial effects from physical and transition risks

name: Own workforce
note: Seventeen disclosure requirements — the largest topical standard in Set 1 by disclosure count, and the one most affected by the simplification. The count is stated; the individual names are not, because they could not be sourced.
dr_source: Count sourced: S1-1 to S1-4 cover impacts, risks and opportunities management and S1-5 to S1-17 cover metrics and targets. The seventeen individual requirement names could not be established from a source reachable here, so they are not enumerated rather than invented. This is the one standard in Set 1 this tool still tracks at standard level.
